questions.stem: A metal rod of square cross-sectional area A having length l has current I flowing through it when a potential difference of V volt is applied across its ends (figure 1). Now, the rod is cut parallel to its length into two identical pieces and joined as shown in Figure II. What potential difference must be maintained across the length of 2l , so that the current in the rod is still I ? {{IMG_BLOCK:https://examcdn.trogon.info/qai/2026/09/26/ba5e7934-50a8-40ec-b02e-b8078927fc94_12CBCH-3CurrentElectricityDPP/b64820b73596.png}}

(i) When the rod is cut parallel and rejoined, the length of the conductor becomes 2l , whereas the area decreases to $\frac{A}{2}$ . If the current remains 2 the same, then the potential changes as V = I$\rho$ $\frac{2\text}{ l}{\text{A}}$ = 4 × I$\rho$ $\frac{l}{A}$ = 4 V [using Eq.(i)] The new potential applied across the metal rod will be four times the original potential (V).

questions.stem: Explain how electron mobility changes for a good conductor, when:

sub_parts.a: the temperature of the conductor is decreased at constant potential difference, and
sub_parts.b: applied potential difference is doubled at constant temperature.

questions.answer_text: The mobility of the charge carrier is the drift velocity acquired by it in a unit electric field. $\mu$ = $\frac{vd}{E}$ … . (i) v_{d} = $\frac{qE\tau }{m}$ … . (ii) From eqn (i) and (ii) we get, ∴ $\mu$ = $\frac{q\tau }{m}$ For electrons, $\mu$ _{e} = $\frac{e\tau e}{m}$ (a) When temperature of the conductor decreases, the relaxation time_{e} $\tau$ of the electrons in the conductor increases, So mobility increases. (b) Mobility is the independent of the applied potential difference.

(b) Mobility is the independent of the applied potential difference.

sub_parts.a: Define the term 'conductivity' of a metallic wire. Write its SI unit.
sub_parts.b: Using the concept of free electrons in a conductor, derive the expression for the conductivity of a wire in terms of number density and relaxation time. Hence, obtain the relation between current density and the applied electric field E. [3 marks]

questions.answer_text: (a) Conductivity of a metallic wire is defined as its ability to allow electric charges or heat to pass through it. Numerically, conductivity of a material is reciprocal of its resistivity._{−1} SI unit: ohm^{−1} m or mho m^{−1} or Siemen^{−1} m (b) Consider a potential difference V be applied across a conductor of length I and cross section A . Electric field inside the conductor, E = $\frac{V}{l}$ Due to the external field the free electrons inside the conductor drift with velocity v_{d} . Let, number of electrons per unit volume = n , charge on an electron = e Total electrons in length, l = nAl and, total charge, q = neAl {{IMG_BLOCK:https://examcdn.trogon.info/qai/2026/09/26/ba5e7934-50a8-40ec-b02e-b8078927fc94_12CBCH-3CurrentElectricityDPP/af536e6e91e0.png}} And current, I = $\frac{q}{t}$ I = $\frac{neAl}{l}$ v_{d} I = neAv_{d} Therefore, current per unit area, i.e., current density J = $\frac{I}{A}$ = nev_{d} J = ne( $\frac{eE\tau }{m}$ ) = ( $\frac{ne\tau }{m}$ )E^{2} J = $\sigma$ E which is the required expression.
